accepted_examples.german: Wir wollen unser Geld sinnvoll einsetzen.
accepted_examples.english: We want to put our money to good use.
accepted_examples.note: Verified adjective use and practical useful/appropriate sense; translation is idiomatic.

accepted_examples.german: Tom spülte die Teekanne mit heißem Wasser aus.
accepted_examples.english: Tom rinsed the teapot with hot water.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the separable verb and rinsing sense; translation is accurate.
Verified the adverbial adjective use and methodical sense.
Verified the adverb and partial-extent sense; translation is direct.

accepted_examples.german: Die Änderung wird tiefgreifende Folgen für das System nach sich ziehen.
accepted_examples.english: The change will lead to profound consequences for the system.
accepted_examples.note: Verified adjective inflection and wide-impact sense; translation is faithful.

accepted_examples.german: Tom wusste, dass es falsch war, was er tat, aber er tat es trotzdem.
accepted_examples.english: Tom knew what he was doing was wrong, but he did it anyway.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the contrastive adverb and natural English equivalent.

accepted_examples.german: Am Montag beginnen umfangreiche Arbeiten an der Autobahnbrücke.
accepted_examples.english: On Monday, extensive work begins at the motorway bridge.
accepted_examples.note: Verified adjective agreement and extensive-scale sense; translation is accurate.

accepted_examples.german: Glauben Sie, Sie können Ihre Idee in die Praxis umsetzen?
accepted_examples.english: Do you think that you can put your idea into practice?
accepted_examples.note: Verified the separable verb and implementation sense; this pair illustrates the target well.

accepted_examples.german: Ich hoffe, dass du deine Behauptungen auch mit Beweisen untermauern kannst.
accepted_examples.english: I hope you've got some proof to back up your allegations.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the verb construction and evidence-support sense; the translation matches.
Verified the adjective and required/not-optional sense, including negation.

accepted_examples.german: Der Mond ist nicht immer gleich weit von der Erde entfernt.
accepted_examples.english: The moon is not always the same distance away from Earth.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the spatial-distance sense and translation.

accepted_examples.german: Englisch ist eine Sprache, die weltweit gesprochen wird.
accepted_examples.english: English is a language spoken all over the world.
accepted_examples.note: Verified adverb use and the worldwide-distribution sense.

accepted_examples.german: Lassen Sie mich kurz zusammenfassen, was passiert ist!
accepted_examples.english: Let me briefly summarize what happened.
accepted_examples.note: Verified formal imperative, separable verb form, and summary sense.

accepted_examples.german: Tom sagte Maria, daß er Johannes für zuverlässig halte.
accepted_examples.english: Tom told Mary that he thought John was dependable.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the adjective and dependable-person sense; retained the attributed source pair.

accepted_examples.english: A surprising number of interested people came.
accepted_examples.note: Verified the adverbial adjective and unexpected high quantity sense.

accepted_examples.english: The students are for the most part diligent.
accepted_examples.note: Verified adverb use and mostly/for-the-greater-part sense.

editorial_examples.german: Während des Fotos musste die Gruppe kurz stillstehen.
editorial_examples.english: The group had to stand still briefly during the photo.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a mistranslated source pair; the new sentence demonstrates remaining motionless.

editorial_examples.german: Über den letzten Punkt ist noch nicht entschieden; er bleibt strittig.
editorial_examples.english: The final point has not been decided yet; it remains disputed.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a machine-translated sentence with idiomatic English and a clear dispute sense.

editorial_examples.german: Die Bewertung ist subjektiv und hängt von persönlichen Vorlieben ab.
editorial_examples.english: The assessment is subjective and depends on personal preferences.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a translation with adjective-agreement errors and made the personal-opinion sense explicit.

editorial_examples.german: Gute Kommunikation ist für das Projekt unabdingbar.
editorial_examples.english: Good communication is essential for the project.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a broad factual claim with a neutral example of something indispensable.

editorial_examples.german: Die beiden Aufgaben sind unterschiedlich schwierig.
editorial_examples.english: The two tasks differ in difficulty.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced an elliptical example with a complete, concise sentence showing a clear difference.
Replaced an awkward machine translation with a concise visual-explanation example.

editorial_examples.german: Die neue Anleitung vereinfacht den Vorgang.
editorial_examples.english: The new instructions simplify the process.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a tense-mismatched and context-free example with a clear practical use.

editorial_examples.german: Die neuen Daten widerlegen diese Theorie.
editorial_examples.english: The new data disproves this theory.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a passive personal reaction with a direct transitive example of disproving a claim.

editorial_examples.english: I'm afraid I have to disagree with you.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a punctuation issue with a concise example that also demonstrates the dative object.

editorial_examples.german: Ich schicke dir die Unterlagen morgen zu.
editorial_examples.english: I'll send you the documents tomorrow.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a sentence using schicken rather than the target lemma zuschicken.
Replaced a machine-translated English gloss that gave the wrong sense.
